citation.title: Fast topology optimization of phononic crystal-based metastructures for vibration isolation by deep learning
citation.authors: Chen-Xu Liu, Gui-Lan Yu, Zhanli Liu
citation.venue: Computer-Aided Civil and Infrastructure Engineering (OpenAlex and audit/pool/pool.csv give the online-publication date as 2023-09-30; a secondary web-search citation snippet gives the print issue as 2024, vol. 39(5), pp. 776-790 -- not independently confirmed since the full text/publisher page could not be opened)
citation.version_coded: No version of the full text was accessible. Coded from the abstract, reconstructed from OpenAlex's stored metadata (api.openalex.org/works/https://doi.org/10.1111/mice.13100, work id W4387222506) and cross-checked word-for-word against the abstract already stored in audit/pool/pool.csv for this pid (identical).

included.reason: I-SPEED (abstract states an explicit quantitative speed comparison with a classical genetic algorithm: 'only requires 0.01% of the time GA costs'). Elastic-wave/phononic metamaterial design in solids is in scope per the PROTOCOL section-11 deviation on physics scope ('acoustic' in section 4 means sound in fluids; elastic-wave/phononic/seismic metamaterial design is elasticity and in scope)

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: DLBO, a deep-learning-based optimization method for phononic-crystal metastructure topology, is reported to achieve bandgap results similar to or better than a genetic algorithm while needing only about 0.01% of the genetic algorithm's computation time.
claim.key_phrase: only requires 0.01% of the time GA costs
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Abstract states DLBO 'only requires 0.01% of the time GA costs'; 1/0.0001 = 10,000x, taken directly as stated. No other numeric figures are available since the full text could not be accessed, so this cannot be cross-checked against a derivation from raw times.
claim.alternatives: The abstract also frames the same comparison qualitatively ('achieves similar or better results to genetic algorithm (GA)') and separately reports an application-validation claim (an economical metastructure customized for subway-induced vibrations, verified with a 3D finite element model) with no comparator or numbers attached. Full text is inaccessible, so introduction/conclusion/results sections could not be checked for other candidate primary outcomes.

baseline.classical_method: Genetic algorithm (GA), per the abstract; no further detail (encoding, population size, fitness function) is available without full text
baseline.problem_size: not stated in the abstract beyond 'metastructures with different periodic constants and filling fractions'
baseline.classical_time: not stated in absolute terms; only the relative figure '0.01% of the time GA costs' is given
baseline.ml_time: not stated in absolute terms; see claimed_speedup_basis
baseline.data_generation_cost: not stated (abstract only); abstract states DLBO 'eliminates the need for pre-optimized data', which may mean training data are generated differently from a conventional supervised pipeline, but the mechanism is not described in the abstract
baseline.quality_metric: not stated precisely; abstract says DLBO 'achieves similar or better results' than GA on bandgap-related objectives, and that a customized metastructure's vibration-isolation performance 'is verified through a 3D finite element model'
baseline.quality_gap: not stated numerically in the abstract

reporting.n_test_cases: not stated in the abstract; full text inaccessible
